D01: Meals on domestic travel: the daily meal allowance is USD 75 for each full travel day. Departure and return days count as travel days and are reimbursed at 75 percent of the daily allowance.
D02: Flights and hotels must be booked through TravelDesk, the corporate booking tool. Bookings made outside TravelDesk need a written exception from Finance.
D03: Current hotel nightly caps (2026 travel policy): London GBP 260, New York USD 340, Chicago USD 280, Tokyo JPY 32000. Lodging above the cap is not reimbursable.
D04: Archived 2024 lodging rates (superseded, kept for audit): London GBP 220, New York USD 300, Chicago USD 250, Tokyo JPY 28000.
D05: Expense reports must be submitted within 30 calendar days of the trip end date.
D06: Late expense reports need director sign-off and are reimbursed at 90 percent, unless the delay was caused by a TravelDesk or expense-system outage. A documented outage extends the submission deadline by the length of the outage.
D07: System status log: TravelDesk was unavailable from March 20 to March 24 inclusive (5 days).
D08: Cabin class: business class is permitted when the scheduled flight time exceeds 6 hours for employees in Band B or above. All other employees fly economy.
D09: Job architecture: Associates and Senior Associates are Band A; Leads and Principals are Band B; Directors and VPs are Band C.
D10: Band C employees receive 125 percent of the city hotel cap on all trips.
D11: Pre-approval thresholds: under USD 500 manager approval; USD 500 to 2000 director approval; above USD 2000 VP approval.
D12: Conference registration fees above USD 1500 always require VP approval, regardless of the general thresholds.
D13: Personal car mileage is reimbursed at USD 0.67 per mile. Tolls and parking are reimbursed at cost.
D14: Flight changes made within 24 hours of departure require manager approval. Red-eye flights over 5 hours allow a late start the next day.
D15: Employees traveling more than 10 days per month may join the frequent-traveler program for lounge access.
D16: Hotel loyalty points earned on business trips may be kept by employees. Hotel upgrades must not increase the nightly cost.
D17: Engineering offsites: engineers may fly premium economy on flights longer than 4 hours when the offsite budget allows.
D18: Long flights: for any flight over 9 hours, employees may book a hotel day room on arrival.
